findings.title: Gate C's ✅ 'live MangaDex read proven end-to-end' executes zero lines of Rust
findings.detail: §0a marks the live read ✅ 'proven end-to-end (logic) against a live v2.3.2243 engine … 5/5 assertions'. The harness substitutes BOTH ends. Hosted is a mock (`harness.entry.ts:makeMockHosted`, used at harness.entry.ts:219). The Tauri IPC boundary is `tauri-core-stub.mjs`, which hard-codes `invoke('suwayomi_status') -> {state:'ready', version:'v2.3.2243'}` (tauri-core-stub.mjs:7-9) and implements `invoke('suwayomi_image')` as a bare `fetch(BASE+args.path)` (:20-24). So the harness never exercises `validate_image_path`, the `image_fetch_semaphore()` cap, the 32 MiB body ceiling, the supervisor's `base_url()` gating, or the `tauri::ipc::Response` byte-transfer shape — every one of which sits between the proven TypeScript and a real device. The 'real JPEG (376 KB, FF D8 FF)' evidence is a Node fetch of the engine, not proof the Rust command returns those bytes to the WebView. Additionally assertion E can degrade to `[SKIP]` (harness.entry.ts:283-285) without failing, so '5/5' may be 4 asserts plus a skip.
findings.failure_scenario: `validate_image_path` rejects a path shape the engine actually emits (e.g. a query string on `/api/v1/manga/3/chapter/1/page/0?...`), or the `MAX_CONCURRENT_IMAGE_FETCHES=6` semaphore deadlocks under the reader's `Promise.all`-every-page prefetch. The harness passes 5/5 because it never calls the Rust command; the app shows a blank chapter on device.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a Rust-side integration test (runnable in the existing x86_64-linux CI leg, which already has the jar+JRE) that boots the engine via `boot_engine` and then calls the real `suwayomi_image` handler path for a known `/api/v1/...` route, asserting JPEG magic on the returned bytes. Separately, make assertion E a hard fail or an explicit expected-skip list rather than a silent pass.

Both live under `apps/reader/src-tauri/e2e/` — which IS inside native-sidecar.yml's path filter (native-sidecar.yml:18, `apps/reader/src-tauri/**`) — yet no step in either workflow invokes them; `grep -rn 'e2e/' .github/workflows/` matches only the unrelated Playwright project in ci.yml:167,218. Note also that changes to `packages/api/**` do not even trigger native-sidecar.yml, so the fallback ladder and offline queue have no gate on the path where their code actually lives.

findings.fix_sketch: Add an `ubuntu-latest` job (in ci.yml so it triggers on packages/api changes, not just src-tauri) that runs `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` then both `run-fallback-check.sh` and `run-offline-check.sh`. findings.title: §0a's 🟡 'unit-covered accounting' for kill→degraded+restart is false — the supervision loop has zero tests
findings.detail: §0a's Gate C line reads '🟡 kill→degraded+restart (implemented + unit-covered accounting; live kill not automated)', implying the restart accounting is at least unit-tested even though the live kill is not. It is not. `grep -n 'MAX_RESTARTS_PER_MIN\|storm' apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi.rs` returns only lines 41, 42, 443, 444 and 460 — all inside `supervise_loop` (suwayomi.rs:387-465); the `#[cfg(test)]` module at suwayomi.rs:750-888 contains no reference to any of them. The only adjacent test, `state_transitions_drive_base_url_and_status` (suwayomi.rs:806-828), calls the pure `set_ready`/`transition` setters directly and never touches the 60 s trailing-window `VecDeque`, the `restarts.len() > MAX_RESTARTS_PER_MIN` storm trip, or the `(2 * restarts.len()).min(30)` backoff curve. So the ONE degraded-path behaviour the 🟡 admits is risky is also the one with no coverage at all.
findings.failure_scenario: An off-by-one or a mis-ordered `restarts.clear()` (suwayomi.rs:461) makes the storm branch unreachable, so a crash-looping JVM is respawned every 2 s forever — draining battery and pegging CPU on a mobile device — with no test anywhere that would notice, and §0a still advertising the accounting as unit-covered.
findings.fix_sketch: Extract the window/backoff decision into a pure `fn next_backoff(restarts: &mut VecDeque<Instant>, now: Instant) -> (Duration, bool)` (mirroring the injectable `acquire_boot_port` pattern already used in suwayomi_ios.rs:775-843) and unit-test the storm trip, the cap at 30 s, and the window eviction. Runs offline inside the existing `cargo test --lib` step.

findings.title: image-provider.ts — the user's headline native-image goal — has no automated coverage of any kind

Type-checking via ci.yml's svelte-check is the only thing standing behind this file, and type-checking proves nothing about which provider is chosen or which URL shape is dispatched.

findings.title: The CI sidecar boot smoke has two silent-pass paths and can go green without booting anything
findings.detail: `native-sidecar.yml:128-132` runs `cargo test --lib -- --ignored sidecar_boots` with `KOMIKA_JAVA_BIN`/`KOMIKA_SUWAYOMI_JAR` set from `github.workspace`. Two independent ways this reports success without asserting anything: (1) the test body itself early-`return`s green when either env var is unset or empty (suwayomi.rs:858-866, `_ => return, // skip: env not set`) — a path-typo in the matrix slug or a `jre/` layout change yields a green step; (2) `cargo test` exits 0 when a name filter matches zero tests, so renaming the fn or mistyping the `sidecar_boots` filter also yields a green step. This is the ONLY artifact behind Gate C's '✅ cold-start' and '✅ no orphaned java (proven)' claims, so both claims are one typo away from being vacuous.
findings.failure_scenario: `build-jre.sh` changes its output layout from `jre/<slug>/bin/java` to `jre/<slug>/Contents/Home/bin/java` on macOS. The env var now points at a non-existent path — but it is still non-empty, so the test proceeds and fails loudly. The worse variant: the step is edited to derive the path from a var that resolves empty; the test returns green, and the boot gate silently stops testing anything for months.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace the two `_ => return` skips with `panic!("KOMIKA_JAVA_BIN unset")` when a `CI` env var is present, and change the run line to `cargo test --lib -- --ignored --exact suwayomi::tests::sidecar_boots_and_reports_about_server` so a rename fails the step instead of matching nothing.

findings.title: Gate C's '✅ cold-start <30 s (proven)' is backed by a test with a 60 s budget and no timing assertion
findings.detail: §0a's scorecard leads with '✅ cold-start `<30 s` + status states (proven)'. The only boot artifact is `sidecar_boots_and_reports_about_server` (suwayomi.rs:857-887), which calls `boot_engine(&cfg, &client, Duration::from_secs(60))` (suwayomi.rs:869) — twice the claimed threshold — and then asserts only `port > 0`, `!version.is_empty()`, that `server.conf` contains `kcefEnabled = false`, and that the child exited. It never records or asserts elapsed time. A 55-second cold start on the slowest CI runner passes this test while flatly violating the ✅ claim. (The sibling android-jdk-probe DOES record a cold-start figure — `run.sh` prints `cold-start: ${COLD}s` — so the pattern exists in the repo; the desktop gate just doesn't use it.)
findings.failure_scenario: A jar bump or a jlink module-set change pushes cold start from 4 s to 45 s. CI stays green, §0a keeps claiming <30 s, and users see a 45-second dead engine on every launch with the status stuck in `starting`.
findings.fix_sketch: In the test, wrap `boot_engine` in `let t0 = Instant::now();` / `assert!(t0.elapsed() < Duration::from_secs(30), "cold start {:?} exceeds Gate C budget", t0.elapsed());` and drop the boot budget to 30 s so the claim and the code agree. Echo the measured value into `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` like the JRE-size step already does.

findings.title: N2.1 'curl+harness-verified' extension provisioning has no repeatable check, and the workflow's own TODO admits the gap
findings.detail: §0a lists N2.1 as complete and 'curl+harness-verified'. There is no deterministic artifact: the install-once/in-flight-dedupe logic in `local-suwayomi-backend.ts` is exercised only inside `e2e/native-read/run.sh` (which requires the gitignored 174 MB jar, a jlink'd JRE, and live egress to Keiyoushi + MangaDex — see its own header at run.sh:4-6) and inside `e2e/android-jdk-probe/run.sh` (Docker + network). Neither is in CI. `native-sidecar.yml:135-146` even carries an explicit `TODO(N2.1): chapter-list smoke … DELIBERATELY NOT IMPLEMENTED here and asserts nothing today`, correctly refusing to add a fake-green placeholder — but that TODO has not been discharged even though N2.1 is now marked landed, so the workflow's stated blocker ('requires on-device extension provisioning that does not exist yet') is stale and the gap is permanent.
findings.failure_scenario: The dedupe map keying changes so two concurrent series opens both trigger `installExtension`, and the engine returns a 409 for the second. Nothing in CI installs an extension, so this only surfaces as an intermittent 'no chapters' on a real device.
findings.fix_sketch: Two parts. (a) Add a deterministic in-flight-dedupe check (stubbed `invoke`, no engine) alongside the fallback-ladder check — asserts one `installExtension` for N concurrent `refFor` calls. (b) Discharge the workflow TODO on the x86_64-linux leg only, where the jar and JRE are already present: addRepo -> fetchExtensions -> installExtension -> fetchSourceManga -> assert non-empty, marked `continue-on-error: false` but network-flake-tolerant via a retry.

findings.title: N-CF's 'live setSettings acceptance against v2.3.2243' is a one-off manual run with no artifact
findings.detail: §0a states N-CF is 'Verified: shim protocol + engine-fallback contract + loopback health (7 tests), live `setSettings` acceptance against v2.3.2243.' The 7 tests are real and CI-gated (cloudflare.rs:617-801, run by native-sidecar.yml:119-120), but they all test the shim in isolation — `handle_v1_*`, serde round-trips, loopback binding. The one claim that spans the shim-to-engine boundary, that a real v2.3.2243 accepts `setSettings(flareSolverrUrl=<shim>)`, has no test, no recorded transcript in `N-CF-SPIKE-FINDINGS.md`, and no CI step. This is the assertion that the entire on-device Cloudflare strategy hinges on, and it is the only one not mechanised — despite `native-sidecar.yml:128-132` already having a booted, real v2.3.2243 in hand at that exact point in the job.
findings.failure_scenario: A future jar bump renames or removes the `flareSolverrUrl` settings field. The 7 shim tests stay green, the boot smoke stays green, and the CF bypass silently stops being wired to the engine — discovered only when a gated source starts returning challenge HTML to users.
findings.fix_sketch: Extend the existing `#[ignore]`d boot test (or add a sibling) to issue `mutation { setSettings(input:{settings:{flareSolverrEnabled:true, flareSolverrUrl:"http://127.0.0.1:1"}}){...} }` against the booted engine and assert the field round-trips in the response. Costs nothing extra — the engine is already up in that step.

findings.title: Every `could_not_verify` item lives only in Markdown; nothing executable tracks or expires them
findings.detail: The standing unverified set — live CF solve in a WebView with `cf_clearance` replay, per-OS webview UA-override/cookie behaviour, interactive-Turnstile UX, on-device iOS JVM boot, the DOM `` blob paint, a real hosted `workSources` response — is recorded only as prose across native-embedded-suwayomi.md:70,94, n4.1-ios-jvm-findings.md:310, device-verify-runbook.md:3,253,310 and N-CF-SPIKE-FINDINGS.md:272. There is no `#[ignore]`d test, no skipped check, no tracked issue, and no CI annotation for any of them. The repo already demonstrates the better pattern: the `#[ignore]`d `sidecar_boots_and_reports_about_server` is a machine-readable placeholder that a CI job opts into. Prose-tracked items cannot be counted, cannot be surfaced in a job summary, and rot invisibly — device-verify-runbook.md is dated but nothing tells a reader whether it was ever executed.
findings.failure_scenario: Six months on, §0a still says 'Remaining after Wave E spikes: execute the runbook on a display'. Nobody can tell from CI whether that is still true, which items were quietly discharged by a manual run, or which have been invalidated by a jar bump — so the release decision is made on stale prose.
findings.fix_sketch: Convert each item into an `#[ignore = "needs a physical device: see device-verify-runbook.md §N"]` test or a `test.skip()` check that names the runbook section, and add a CI step that prints the ignored-test roster into `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` so the count of outstanding manual verifications is visible on every run.

findings.title: §0a's headline gate counts are stale in three places, so the numbers cannot be used to detect drift
findings.detail: §0a line 17 asserts 'all gates green: reader svelte-check 344/0/0, src-tauri 13/0, server 112/0'. Measured today: reader svelte-check reports 401 FILES (I ran `svelte-kit sync && svelte-check` on this host); src-tauri has 20 non-ignored tests on a desktop target (lib.rs 7 at :287-358, suwayomi.rs 6 at :754-848, cloudflare.rs 7 at :617-801) plus 1 `#[ignore]`d, not 13; apps/server carries 375 `#[test]`/`#[tokio::test]` attributes against a claimed 112. §0a further states N2.3 is a '19-assertion check' where the script actually emits 22 PASS lines. None of these numbers is regenerated by anything, so a reader cannot use them to tell whether coverage grew or a suite silently shrank.
findings.failure_scenario: Someone deletes half the src-tauri tests during a refactor. The count drops from 20 to 10 and still reads as 'better than the documented 13', so the loss is invisible in review and in §0a.
findings.fix_sketch: Either drop the raw counts from §0a in favour of a link to the workflow, or emit them mechanically — `cargo test --lib 2>&1 | tail -1` and the svelte-check `COMPLETED n FILES` line appended to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` — so the authoritative numbers live in the run, not in prose.

audit2.claimed_status: `docs/plans/native-embedded-suwayomi.md` §0a (Wave D) claims N-CF is COMPLETE and "fork-avoidable": "a loopback Rust FlareSolverr-v1 shim + Tauri-WebView solver, wired via `setSettings(flareSolverrUrl=<shim>)` on engine ready; stock Suwayomi injects `cf_clearance`/UA, no fork. Verified: shim protocol + engine-fallback contract + loopback health (7 tests), live `setSettings` acceptance against v2.3.2243." The only admitted `could_not_verify` items are a live challenge solve, per-OS webview UA-override/cookie-read behaviour, and the interactive-Turnstile UX. `apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:12-18` further claims a deliberate trust model where "the shim binds 127.0.0.1 only and only the loopback engine calls it", and `:360-364` claims the solve "can never hang the shim".
audit2.actual_status: Desktop-only prototype with two real protocol defects and one budget mismatch that together make the on-device CF path unlikely to ever deliver a successful read, plus an unauthenticated local API. I pulled the authoritative engine source for the pin (`Suwayomi-Server` v2.3.2243 `eu/kanade/tachiyomi/network/interceptor/CloudflareInterceptor.kt`) and diffed it against the shim. The command set (`request.get`/`request.post` only, no `sessions.*`), the envelope keys, the `awaitSuccess()` HTTP-200 requirement, the `"not detected"` sentinel and the non-2xx→`CloudflareBypassException` fallback contract are all correct — that part of the claim holds. But: (a) the engine's `FlareSolverSolutionCookie.domain` is a NON-NULLABLE `String` while `FsCookie.domain` is `Option<String>` serialized as `null`; (b) the `cookie` crate's `Cookie::domain()` strips the leading dot, and the engine's `if (!cookie.domain.startsWith('.')) it.hostOnlyDomain(...)` therefore downgrades every injected `cf_clearance` to a host-only cookie, so it never covers the subdomains most sources serve pages from; (c) the shim's 45 s wall cap and 8 s interactive grace both exceed the 30 s `HTTP_TIMEOUT` on the reqwest client that carries `suwayomi_gql`, and a timeout there makes `composite-backend.ts` memo the work `localUnusable` and serve it from the hosted proxy for the rest of the session — so a slow-but-successful solve still degrades to the hosted path. The solver also returns any pre-existing `cf_clearance` from the shared WebView jar without invalidating it, which is exactly the cookie the engine just had rejected (re-challenge loop). Security: the loopback listener has no token/nonce, so any local process (or a compromised in-app WebView) can drive it as a "navigate the app's WebView to URL X and hand me every cookie in the shared jar for X" oracle, and can force a visible window over the app after 8 s; the body read is unbounded and on the serving thread, which both DoSes the shim and makes `shutdown()`'s `join()` hang forever (Drop runs at app quit). Platform reality: `mod cloudflare` is `#[cfg(desktop)]` (lib.rs:16-17) and `suwayomi_ios.rs:293` hard-writes `flareSolverrEnabled = false` with nothing ever enabling it, so on iOS/Android the interceptor throws `IOException("Cloudflare bypass currently disabled")` on the FIRST 403/503+cloudflare response; the reader silently marks the work unusable on-device and falls back to `hosted.canonicalPages` — reintroducing the exact server dependency the goal removes, for every CF-gated source, permanently. One positive: the challenge windows get no Tauri capabilities (`capabilities/default.json` scopes to `windows: ["main"]`), so a remote challenge page cannot reach `fetch_image`/`suwayomi_gql` over IPC; and the shim's unit tests DO run in CI on all three desktop OSes (`native-sidecar.yml:120`), unlike the iOS module.
evidence: Authoritative engine contract fetched for the pin: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Suwayomi/Suwayomi-Server/v2.3.2243/server/src/main/kotlin/eu/kanade/tachiyomi/network/interceptor/CloudflareInterceptor.kt — `FlareSolverSolutionCookie(val name: String, val value: String, val domain: String, ...)` (domain NON-nullable); `requestWithFlareSolverr` does `.domain(cookie.domain.removePrefix("."))` then `if (!cookie.domain.startsWith('.')) it.hostOnlyDomain(...)`; the FlareSolverr call is wrapped in `mutex.withLock` (engine self-serialises all solves) and uses `callTimeout(flareSolverrTimeout + 10s)`.

Command set confirmed: the engine only ever sends `"request.${originalRequest.method.lowercase()}"` — it never calls `sessions.create`/`sessions.destroy`, so the shim ignoring `session`/`session_ttl_minutes` is NOT a divergence. `awaitSuccess()` requires HTTP 2xx from the shim; the shim always answers 200 on `/v1` (cloudflare.rs:308-313, 351-357), so the error envelope reaches `requestWithFlareSolverr`, which throws on non-2xx `solution.status` — the documented fallback contract is genuinely correct.

`cookie` crate dot-stripping proven locally: ~/.cargo/registry/src/index.crates.io-*/cookie-0.18.1/src/lib.rs:777-785 `pub fn domain(&self) -> Option<&str> { ... domain.strip_prefix(".").or(Some(domain)) }` — so `to_fs_cookies` (cloudflare.rs:513-526) can never emit a leading-dot domain.

wry cookie sources: webkitgtk/mod.rs:938 sets domain only `if let Some(domain) = cookie.domain()` (can be absent → `FsCookie.domain = None` → serialized `null`); wkwebview/mod.rs:1064 and webview2/mod.rs:1524-1526 always set one.

Budget mismatch: cloudflare.rs:51 `MAX_SOLVE_WALL_MS = 45_000` and :55 `INTERACTIVE_GRACE = 8s` vs apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi.rs:35 `HTTP_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_secs(30)` used at suwayomi.rs:123 for the client behind `suwayomi_gql`.

Fallback trace: packages/api/src/composite-backend.ts:404 `this.localUnusable.add(String(workId))` on any local throw, and :429 `return this.opts.hosted.canonicalPages!(chapterId)` — a CF failure permanently routes that work to the hosted proxy for the session.

Platform gating: apps/reader/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:16-17 `#[cfg(desktop)] mod cloudflare;`; apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi_ios.rs:293 writes `server.flareSolverrEnabled = false`; grep finds no `apply_settings`/`flareSolverr` enablement anywhere outside `suwayomi.rs`. Tauri 2.11.5 webview/mod.rs:2167-2169 documents `cookies()` as "**Android**: Unsupported, always returns an empty Vec".

Capability containment verified (positive): apps/reader/src-tauri/capabilities/default.json is `{"windows": ["main"], "permissions": ["core:default"]}` — the `komika-cf-N` challenge windows get no permissions, so the untrusted challenge origin has no IPC reach.

tiny_http 0.12 behaviour checked in-registry: per-connection reader threads (src/lib.rs:288,323) but the BODY is read by the consumer (`request.as_reader()`), i.e. on `serve_loop`'s thread; `unblock()` only ends `incoming_requests()` (src/lib.rs:409) and cannot interrupt a thread parked inside `read_to_string`. `Drop for Request` (src/request.rs:488-497) emits a 500, so a dropped task does not wedge the socket.

Tauri async runtime is `TokioRuntime::new()` (multi-thread, worker count = cores) — async_runtime.rs:222-223 — so the blocking `recv_timeout`/`cookies_for_url` calls consume shared workers used by every Tauri async command.

CI: .github/workflows/native-sidecar.yml:116-120 runs `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo test --lib` on macOS/Linux/Windows, so the 7 cloudflare.rs unit tests do execute — but none of them POSTs a real `/v1` over the socket or asserts the engine's cookie-shape contract.

findings.title: Solver returns the already-rejected cf_clearance from the shared WebView jar, producing a re-challenge loop
findings.detail: `poll_for_clearance` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:485-496) returns on the FIRST iteration if `cookies_for_url` already contains a cookie named `cf_clearance` — it never invalidates the domain's existing clearance before navigating, never compares against a pre-solve snapshot, and never checks that the cookie post-dates the solve. Tauri's default WebContext persists cookies for the app's lifetime (and on disk across runs), and the engine only calls the shim BECAUSE its own `cf_clearance` was just rejected with a 403/503 (v2.3.2243 CloudflareInterceptor.kt: `code in [403,503] && header("Server") in ["cloudflare-nginx","cloudflare"]`). Since the WebView copy is the same server-invalidated token (CF invalidates clearance server-side on IP/policy change while the cookie's local Max-Age is still far in the future), the shim hands back the dead cookie in ~0 ms, the engine injects it (CFClearance.requestWithFlareSolverr) and replays, gets 403 again, and re-enters the interceptor. Nothing in cloudflare.rs or suwayomi.rs breaks this cycle.
findings.failure_scenario: User reads a CF-gated source on Monday (clearance solved and cached in the WebView jar). On Tuesday the ISP rotates their IP, invalidating the clearance. The engine 403s, calls POST /v1; the shim finds the stale `cf_clearance` in the WebView store on poll #1 and returns it as a fresh solve; the engine replays and 403s again; repeat. The user sees a spinner and the app hammers the source with a hot loop of failing requests instead of ever opening a challenge window.
findings.fix_sketch: Before `build_challenge_window`, snapshot/delete the target domain's `cf_clearance` (Tauri exposes `WebviewWindow::delete_cookie`, or `clear_all_browsing_data` scoped to a throwaway WebContext per solve). Then require that the returned cookie is either absent-then-present, or has a value different from the snapshot, before treating it as solved. Add a unit test with a fake cookie store asserting the pre-existing-cookie case does NOT short-circuit.

findings.title: Leading dot stripped from cookie domains makes the engine mark cf_clearance host-only, so subdomain page hosts stay blocked
findings.detail: `to_fs_cookies` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:513-526, domain at :520) emits `c.domain()` verbatim, but the `cookie` crate deliberately strips a leading dot: cookie-0.18.1/src/lib.rs:777-785 returns `domain.strip_prefix(".").or(Some(domain))`. The pinned engine (Suwayomi-Server v2.3.2243, CloudflareInterceptor.kt `CFClearance.requestWithFlareSolverr`) branches on exactly that dot: `.domain(cookie.domain.removePrefix("."))` … `if (!cookie.domain.startsWith('.')) { it.hostOnlyDomain(cookie.domain.removePrefix(".")) }`. Real FlareSolverr sources its cookies from CDP, which preserves `.example.com`, so upstream gets a domain-match cookie; our shim can never produce one, so EVERY injected cookie becomes host-only. CF sets `cf_clearance` with `Domain=.<apex>` precisely so it covers subdomains, and manga sources routinely serve chapter pages/images from `cdn.`/`img1.`/`s3.` subdomains of the gated apex.
findings.failure_scenario: Source gates `example.org` and serves page images from `img1.example.org`. The shim solves the challenge on `example.org` and returns `domain: "example.org"`; the engine stores it as host-only. The subsequent page-image GET to `img1.example.org` carries no `cf_clearance`, 403s with `Server: cloudflare`, re-enters the interceptor, re-solves on the image URL, and again produces a host-only cookie for `img1.example.org` — every distinct image host costs a full solve, and any host the WebView can't be navigated to never resolves.
findings.fix_sketch: In `to_fs_cookies`, re-prefix a dot for domain-scoped cookies. Minimal correct version: for `cf_clearance` (which CF always sets as a domain cookie) emit `format!(".{}", d)`; better, compare `c.domain()` against the request host and emit a dot whenever the cookie domain is a proper suffix of the host. Add a unit test asserting `solution.cookies[0].domain` starts with '.' for cf_clearance.

findings.title: 45 s solve cap (and 8 s interactive grace) exceed the 30 s GraphQL transport timeout, so a successful solve still degrades the work to the hosted proxy
findings.detail: The shim clamps a solve to `MAX_SOLVE_WALL_MS = 45_000` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:51) and only surfaces an interactive window after `INTERACTIVE_GRACE = 8s` (:55), while the engine's own budget is `flareSolverrTimeout + 10s` = 70 s (CloudflareInterceptor.kt `callTimeout`). But the call that carries the whole thing to the UI is `suwayomi_gql`, which uses the supervisor's reqwest client built with `HTTP_TIMEOUT = Duration::from_secs(30)` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi.rs:35, applied at :123). The engine only answers the GraphQL request AFTER the interceptor's solve+replay completes, so any solve past 30 s makes `suwayomi_gql` return `Err` even though the engine goes on to succeed. In `packages/api/src/composite-backend.ts:399-407` that `Err` lands in the `catch` around `refFor`/`chapters` and does `this.localUnusable.add(String(workId))`, permanently routing that work to `hosted.canonicalPages` (:429) for the rest of the session. There is no retry after the solve lands.
findings.failure_scenario: CF issues an interactive Turnstile for a source. The window is hidden for 8 s, shown, the user takes 15 s to notice and click, clearance appears at ~28-40 s. If it lands after 30 s the IPC call has already failed; the work is memoed unusable and every page in that chapter is fetched from the hosted proxy — while the engine sits there holding a perfectly good cf_clearance nobody will use until the app restarts. Even at 25 s the whole read is one 25 s stall with no UI feedback.
findings.fix_sketch: Make the timeout ladder monotonic: shim wall cap < engine callTimeout < transport timeout. Either raise `HTTP_TIMEOUT` (or use a longer per-call timeout for content queries) above the 70 s engine budget, or drop `MAX_SOLVE_WALL_MS` well under 30 s for the hidden phase and move the interactive phase off the request path (return an error immediately, solve in the background, and let the next attempt succeed). Also stop memoing `localUnusable` on transport timeouts specifically.

findings.title: Loopback /v1 has no token: any local process can navigate the app's WebView to an arbitrary URL and read back its cookie jar
findings.detail: `handle_request` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:318-358) authenticates nothing — no shared secret, no nonce, no Origin/Host check. The only containment is the loopback bind (:41) and the OS-ephemeral port, plus a `GET /` health route that helpfully self-identifies as `komika-cf-shim` (:328-331) and makes port discovery a 64 k-probe scan. `solve_in_webview` (:429-446) validates only the URL scheme (http/https) — no host allowlist, no relation to any configured source — then navigates a real WebView to it and `to_fs_cookies` (:513-526) returns EVERY cookie the shared WebContext jar holds for that URL, not just `cf_clearance`. So the endpoint is a generic 'dump the app's cookies for URL X' oracle for any third-party site the user has logged into inside the app, and a 'render attacker HTML in a window titled "Verifying your connection…" owned by Komiq' primitive after the 8 s grace (:503-506). The shim also starts for every desktop user regardless of `PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi.rs:590-597), so the surface is always live. Mitigating facts I verified: `capabilities/default.json` scopes permissions to `windows: ["main"]`, so the challenge origin gets no Tauri IPC; and a cross-origin browser page can POST but cannot read the response (no CORS headers), leaving it with the window-spoofing/navigation side effect only.
findings.failure_scenario: Any unprivileged process on the user's machine (or a malicious npm/pip postinstall) scans loopback for the `komika-cf-shim` banner, then POSTs `{"cmd":"request.get","url":"https://<source-with-user-login>/"}` and receives that site's full cookie set, including session cookies, in `solution.cookies`. Repeat per target host. Separately it POSTs an attacker URL and, 8 s later, a credential-phishing page is displayed inside a window that looks like it belongs to Komiq.
findings.fix_sketch: Generate a 128-bit random token at `CfShim::start`, require it as a header (or as `flareSolverrUrl = http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<token>` path segment — the engine appends `/v1` to whatever URL you give it, so a path prefix works with zero engine changes), and constant-time compare. Drop or randomise the health banner. Restrict the solvable URL set to hosts the engine has an installed source for, and filter `to_fs_cookies` to `cf_clearance` + cookies already present in the inbound `cookies[]`. Gate `cloudflare::start` on the native-engine flag.

findings.title: Unbounded, untimed body read on the serving thread head-of-line-blocks the shim and makes shutdown()'s join() hang forever
findings.detail: `handle_request` reads the body with `request.as_reader().read_to_string(&mut body)` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:340-345) on the `komika-cf-shim` serving thread, with no size cap and no socket read timeout (tiny_http sets none by default; I confirmed in-registry that tiny_http 0.12 reads headers on per-connection threads but leaves the body to the consumer). The module comment at :293-296 claims the loop 'does no solving… so a slow solve can never head-of-line-block the next request', but the body read is exactly such a block. Worse, `CfShim::shutdown` (:277-283) does `server.unblock()` then `h.join()`, and `unblock()` only terminates `incoming_requests()` (tiny_http src/lib.rs:409) — it cannot interrupt a thread parked inside `read_to_string`. `Drop for CfShim` (:286-291) calls the same `shutdown()`, so this join runs while the app is quitting.
findings.failure_scenario: A local process opens a socket to the shim and sends `POST /v1 HTTP/1.1` with `Content-Length: 10000000000` then trickles one byte per minute. The serving thread parks in `read_to_string` forever: every real engine solve request queues behind it (CF bypass silently dead), memory grows toward 10 GB, and when the user quits the app, `Drop` → `shutdown()` → `join()` never returns, so Komiq hangs on exit and must be force-killed. A merely-buggy peer (or an aborted connection with an unfinished body) reproduces the hang without malice.
findings.fix_sketch: Cap the read with `.take(64 * 1024)` and set a read timeout on the connection (or read the body inside the spawned task rather than on the serving thread, so the loop is never parked). Make `shutdown()`'s join bounded — `join` on a channel with a deadline, or mark the thread detached and rely on process exit. Add a test that a truncated/oversized body yields a 4xx and leaves the listener responsive.

findings.title: Hardcoded Chrome/124 macOS UA is spoofed onto a WebKit/WebView2 engine and echoed unverified, then globally unified across every source
findings.detail: `CHALLENGE_UA` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:61-62) is a frozen `Chrome/124.0.0.0 Safari/537.36` macOS string. It is set on the challenge window (:460) and echoed verbatim as `solution.userAgent` (:494, :203), and the code never reads `navigator.userAgent` back to confirm the override took — despite the spike's own instruction to do so ('Verify the WebView actually honors the override via navigator.userAgent', apps/reader/src-tauri/suwayomi/N-CF-SPIKE-FINDINGS.md:239) and its own verdict that 'UA unification is the #1 failure mode' (:174-176). Two consequences. (1) Fingerprint mismatch: on macOS/Linux the webview is WebKit and sends no `Sec-CH-UA` client hints while claiming to be Chrome; on Windows WebView2 the client hints say Edge/<real version> while the UA says Chrome 124. CF's challenge JS cross-checks UA against `navigator.userAgentData`/client hints, so the challenge either fails or issues a clearance bound to a fingerprint the engine's OkHttp replay cannot reproduce. (2) Blast radius: the engine's `setUserAgent(flareSolverResponse.solution.userAgent)` callback (CloudflareInterceptor.kt) unifies the UA GLOBALLY, so one CF solve retroactively makes every request to every source — MangaDex included — claim to be a stale Chrome 124 on macOS.
findings.failure_scenario: On Linux, the WebKitGTK challenge window presents `Chrome/124` with no `Sec-CH-UA` header. CF's managed challenge flags the inconsistency and either never issues `cf_clearance` (the shim times out at 45 s and the work is memoed hosted-only) or issues one that fails on replay. Meanwhile the single solve attempt has already flipped the whole engine's UA to Chrome 124, so unrelated MangaDex requests now carry a UA that has been stale for two years.
findings.fix_sketch: After the window is built, `eval("navigator.userAgent")` back through a JS→Rust channel and echo THAT exact string in `solution.userAgent` (falling back to CHALLENGE_UA only if the eval fails). Prefer leaving the webview UA at its native default rather than spoofing Chrome, so UA and client hints agree. If a fixed UA is kept, pin it to the platform's real engine family and add a CI check that it is refreshed.

findings.title: iOS and Android have no CF bypass at all; the first CF-gated response silently and permanently reroutes the work to the hosted proxy
findings.detail: `mod cloudflare` is `#[cfg(desktop)]` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/lib.rs:16-17), so no shim, no solver and no `apply_settings` exist on mobile. The iOS engine writes `server.flareSolverrEnabled = false` into its server.conf (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi_ios.rs:293, asserted at :757) and nothing anywhere flips it. Per the pinned engine source, the interceptor's second statement is `if (!serverConfig.flareSolverrEnabled.value) throw IOException("Cloudflare bypass currently disabled")` — so on mobile a CF-gated source fails immediately, with no attempt and no user-visible reason. Tracing the failure: the throw surfaces as a GraphQL error → `local.chapters(ref)` rejects → `packages/api/src/composite-backend.ts:404` adds the work to `localUnusable` → :429 serves `hosted.canonicalPages`, and the memo short-circuit at :352 means every later open in that session skips the engine entirely. Nothing logs 'we fell back'. Blast radius, as best the code allows: every source behind CF (the majority of non-MangaDex Keiyoushi sources — CF gating is why §8b exists at all) is 100 % hosted-proxy on iOS and Android, i.e. exactly the server dependency the goal is to eliminate, and it is invisible because the fallback is silent and the reader shows a normal, working page.
findings.failure_scenario: On an iPhone with the native engine enabled, the user opens a chapter from a CF-gated source. The engine throws 'Cloudflare bypass currently disabled' on the first request, the app quietly serves every page from `api.komiq.cc`, and nobody — user or telemetry — can tell the embedded engine was bypassed. If the hosted server is down or the user is offline, the read fails outright with no explanation.
findings.fix_sketch: Port the shim to mobile: it is mostly platform-neutral (tiny_http + the FsReq/FsResp mapping + `handle_v1`) — only `WebviewSolver` is desktop-shaped. On iOS, reuse `WKHTTPCookieStore` via wry's existing wkwebview cookie bridge (`cookie_from_wkwebview`), but note Tauri's multi-window story on iOS is unproven and a hidden/off-screen WKWebView may be JS-throttled, so plan for an in-view, user-visible sheet. On Android, Tauri's cookie API is documented as always returning an empty Vec (tauri 2.11.5 webview/mod.rs:2167-2169), so a Kotlin Tauri plugin over `android.webkit.CookieManager` + a `WebViewClient` is mandatory. Until then, at minimum emit a telemetry/log event whenever `localUnusable` is set so the hosted-fallback rate is measurable.

findings.title: setSettings is fire-and-forget after Ready, so any CF request in the startup gap poisons the localUnusable memo for the whole session
findings.detail: The engine is marked Ready and only THEN is `cloudflare::apply_settings` spawned as a detached task (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi.rs:406-414). Content queries can begin the moment `suwayomi_status` reports ready, so there is a race window where `flareSolverrEnabled` is still `false` — the value `render_server_conf` rewrites into server.conf before EVERY launch (suwayomi.rs:239). During that window the interceptor throws 'Cloudflare bypass currently disabled'. `apply_settings` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:557-598) has no retry: on a transport error or an unconfirmed response it only `log::warn!`s, and the desktop lane already established that release builds install no logger, so the entire CF subsystem can be silently inert for the whole run. Because `composite-backend.ts:404` memoizes on ANY local throw, a single request that lands in the gap marks the work unusable on-device permanently for the session.
findings.failure_scenario: The reader restores the last-read chapter on launch. The engine flips to Ready, the reader immediately issues `chapters(ref)` for a CF-gated source, and the interceptor throws because the spawned `setSettings` has not completed its round-trip yet. The work is added to `localUnusable`; even after the shim is wired 40 ms later, that work is hosted-only until the app is restarted.
findings.fix_sketch: Await `apply_settings` (with a bounded retry/backoff) BEFORE transitioning the supervisor state to Ready, or gate `ready_endpoint()`/`suwayomi_status` on a `cf_wired` flag. Surface a hard failure as `Degraded` with a reason rather than a warn-only log, and re-run it on every reconnect.

findings.title: A cookie with no domain serializes as `"domain": null`, which the engine's non-nullable Kotlin field rejects, failing the whole solve
findings.detail: `FsCookie.domain` is `Option<String>` with only `#[serde(default)]` and no `skip_serializing_if` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:72-74), so a `None` is emitted as JSON `null`. The pinned engine declares `data class FlareSolverSolutionCookie(val name: String, val value: String, val domain: String, ...)` — `domain` is NON-nullable, and kotlinx.serialization throws on a null for it, which `parseAs<FlareSolverResponse>()` propagates and `CloudflareInterceptor` rewraps as `IOException`. `to_fs_cookies` returns EVERY cookie for the URL (:513-526), so one domain-less cookie in the jar poisons the entire response, including a perfectly good `cf_clearance`. wry's WebKitGTK path can produce this: webkitgtk/mod.rs:938 only sets a domain `if let Some(domain) = cookie.domain()`. Secondary shape issue in the same function: `expires: None` (a session cookie) makes the engine skip `expiresAt`, so the injected cookie is a session cookie the persistent OkHttp store may not retain across restarts. The claimed 'shim protocol verified' tests (:735-771) only round-trip the shim's OWN serde types — they never assert the engine's nullability contract.
findings.failure_scenario: On Linux, the challenge page sets an analytics cookie whose soup record has no domain. `cookies_for_url` returns it alongside `cf_clearance`; the shim emits `"domain": null` for it; the engine's decoder throws; the interceptor converts a successful solve into an IOException; the work is memoed unusable and served hosted-only.
findings.fix_sketch: Never emit a null domain: fall back to the request URL's host when `c.domain()` is `None`, and/or drop cookies that cannot be given a domain. Add a unit test asserting `solution.cookies[*].domain` is always a non-null string and always dot-prefixed for cf_clearance, documenting it as the engine's hard contract.

findings.title: The solve blocks Tauri's shared async-runtime workers (10 s window build + every cookie poll), and the docs still describe a block_on design that no longer exists
findings.detail: Solves are dispatched with `tauri::async_runtime::spawn` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:351), i.e. onto Tauri's global tokio runtime — which is `TokioRuntime::new()`, a multi-thread runtime sized to the core count (tauri-2.11.5/src/async_runtime.rs:222-223). Inside that async task, `build_challenge_window` does a synchronous `rx.recv_timeout(Duration::from_secs(10))` (:467), blocking a worker for up to 10 s, and `poll_for_clearance` calls the blocking `win.cookies_for_url(...)` (:489) every 400 ms for up to 45 s — each call round-trips to the event-loop thread and parks the worker. Tauri async commands (`suwayomi_gql`, `fetch_image`) run on that same pool. On a 1-2 core machine (or a VM), one solve therefore starves the app's entire IPC layer. Separately, the in-tree documentation is stale and misleading about this exact mechanism: `CfShim::start`'s doc says the solver 'runs off the tokio workers (on the serving thread via block_on)' (:235-236) and apps/reader/src-tauri/Cargo.toml:34-35 says tiny_http 'bridges to the async WebView solver via tauri::async_runtime::block_on' — there is no `block_on` anywhere in the file, so anyone auditing the documented main-thread-deadlock risk is analysing a design that was replaced.
findings.failure_scenario: On a 2-core laptop, a CF solve begins. `recv_timeout` parks worker 1 for up to 10 s; the 400 ms cookie polls park worker 2 repeatedly. Concurrent `suwayomi_gql` / `fetch_image` futures cannot be polled, so covers stop loading and the reader freezes for the duration of the solve even for unrelated, non-CF content.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the blocking sections in `tauri::async_runtime::spawn_blocking` (or convert `build_challenge_window` to an async channel `recv` with `tokio::time::timeout`, and move `cookies_for_url` into `spawn_blocking`). Update the `CfShim::start` doc comment and the Cargo.toml tiny_http rationale to describe the actual spawn-per-request design.

findings.title: No cap on concurrent solves: each /v1 spawns its own hidden WebView window with nothing bounding the total
findings.detail: `handle_request` spawns an unbounded task per `/v1` POST (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:347-357) and each one builds a fresh WebviewWindow with a unique label (:422-425, :451-469). There is no semaphore, no per-host dedupe and no queue depth limit — contrast `lib.rs`'s `MAX_CONCURRENT_IMAGE_FETCHES` semaphore, which the image path does have. In normal operation this is masked by the engine, which serialises all FlareSolverr calls under `mutex.withLock` (verified in CloudflareInterceptor.kt), so at most one solve is in flight from the engine — but that is the ENGINE's property, not the shim's, and the shim is reachable by any local process (see cfshim-unauthenticated-loopback-cookie-oracle). Each hidden window is a full browser instance: hundreds of MB of RSS and GPU/compositor resources.
findings.failure_scenario: A local process fires 200 concurrent `POST /v1` requests with distinct URLs. The shim builds 200 hidden WebViews, each rendering a remote page and polling cookies every 400 ms, until the app OOMs or the window server refuses. Even a friendly caller (a future in-process solver, or an engine version that drops the mutex) reproduces this on a chapter whose pages span many CF-gated hosts.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a `tokio::sync::Semaphore` (1-2 permits) around `solve_bounded`, plus a per-host in-flight map so duplicate solves for the same host share one window and one result. Reject (with a fast error_resp) rather than queue once the depth exceeds a small bound.

findings.title: Inbound seed cookies are discarded, so the challenge is solved in a logged-out context the engine cannot reproduce
findings.detail: The engine faithfully sends the source's existing non-cf cookies (CloudflareInterceptor.kt: `network.cookieStore.get(url).filter { it.name !in COOKIE_NAMES }.map { FlareSolverCookie(it.name, it.value) }`), and the shim parses them into `FsReq.cookies` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:90-91) — then throws them away with `let _ = seed_cookies;` (:413-416), documented as 'Tauri exposes no pre-nav cookie-set API'. That justification is wrong for the current Tauri version: `WebviewWindow::set_cookie` exists in tauri 2.11.5 (webview/mod.rs, right after `cookies_for_url`). Real FlareSolverr injects the seed cookies before navigating, so this is a genuine protocol divergence, not merely a missing nicety. CF's managed challenges and many sources vary the challenge by session/login state, and a source that requires a login cookie to render the gated page will hand the hidden WebView a login wall instead of a challenge.
findings.failure_scenario: A user is logged into a members-only source; the engine holds its `session=` cookie. The engine 403s and forwards `session` as a seed cookie. The shim navigates a cookie-less WebView, which is redirected to /login instead of the challenge page, so `cf_clearance` never appears; the shim burns the full 45 s and returns an error, and the work is memoed hosted-only.
findings.fix_sketch: Set the seed cookies on the challenge webview before/at navigation using `WebviewWindow::set_cookie` (or navigate to `about:blank` first, set cookies, then navigate to the target). Update the comment, which currently records a limitation that no longer holds.

findings.title: The 'protocol verified' test suite never exercises the real /v1 socket path nor the engine's actual cookie contract
findings.detail: The seven tests (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:617-801) cover `handle_v1` with fake solvers, a serde round-trip of the shim's OWN types, the loopback bind constant, and the `GET /` health route. Nothing POSTs a real `/v1` body over the socket, so `handle_request`'s body-read/dispatch/respond path (:318-358) — where the DoS and the 404 routing live — is entirely untested. Nothing asserts the two engine-side contracts I verified against v2.3.2243: `domain` must be non-null (kotlinx non-nullable field) and must retain a leading dot to avoid `hostOnlyDomain`. Nothing tests that a pre-existing cf_clearance must not short-circuit the solve. This matters because CI DOES run these tests on all three desktop OSes (`.github/workflows/native-sidecar.yml:116-120`), so the checks that are missing are cheap to add and would run everywhere — the gap is coverage choice, not infrastructure.
findings.failure_scenario: Any of cfshim-cookie-domain-dot-stripped-host-only, cfshim-null-domain-breaks-engine-deserialization or cfshim-unbounded-body-read-blocks-listener-and-quit is introduced or persists with a fully green `cargo test --lib` on macOS, Linux and Windows, because no test in the suite can observe them.
findings.fix_sketch: Add: (1) an HTTP-level test that POSTs a captured stock-Suwayomi FlareSolverRequest body to the live shim socket and asserts the reply parses and satisfies the engine contract (non-null dot-prefixed domain, `solution.status == 200`, message free of 'not detected'); (2) a test that an oversized/truncated body is rejected quickly and the listener still serves the next request; (3) a fake-cookie-store test asserting a stale cf_clearance is not returned as a fresh solve.

findings.title: The loopback listener opens for every desktop user even when the native-engine flag is off
findings.detail: `cloudflare::start(&app)` is called unconditionally inside `suwayomi::start` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi.rs:590-597), which itself runs for every desktop launch from `lib.rs:256`. `PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE` defaults OFF and only gates JS-side USE of the engine, so users who never enable the native engine still get a permanently listening, unauthenticated loopback HTTP server for the app's whole lifetime. This is the exposure multiplier for cfshim-unauthenticated-loopback-cookie-oracle and cfshim-unbounded-body-read-blocks-listener-and-quit: the attack surface exists on 100 % of desktop installs rather than on the opt-in subset. (The desktop lane's `desktop-engine-always-spawned-regardless-of-flag` covers the JVM side of the same root cause; this is the listener half.)
findings.failure_scenario: A user who has never enabled the native engine runs Komiq. A local process still finds `komika-cf-shim` on loopback and uses it as a cookie oracle / window-spoofing primitive, for a feature the user is not using.
findings.fix_sketch: Read the native-engine flag on the Rust side (env or a config file written by the frontend) and skip both `cloudflare::start` and the supervisor spawn when it is off; or start the shim lazily on the first engine `Ready`.

findings.title: notify_waiters() only cancels solves already parked in the select, so a solve that starts during shutdown runs the full 45 s
findings.detail: `CfShim::shutdown` calls `self.shutdown.notify_waiters()` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:278). `tokio::sync::Notify::notify_waiters` wakes only tasks that have ALREADY registered — it stores no permit — whereas `solve_bounded` registers its waiter lazily inside `tokio::select!` (:378-384). A request whose task is spawned but not yet polled past the select at the moment of notify will never see the signal and will run to `MAX_SOLVE_WALL_MS`. The doc at :274-276 asserts the join is 'now bounded' partly on the strength of this cancellation.
findings.failure_scenario: The user quits Komiq at the exact moment the engine dispatches a solve. The task misses the notification and keeps a hidden WebView polling for 45 s while the app tears down, delaying process exit or leaving a stranded window during teardown.
findings.fix_sketch: Use a `tokio::sync::watch` channel or a `CancellationToken` (level-triggered, so late subscribers observe the already-set state) instead of `Notify::notify_waiters`, and check the flag once at the top of `solve_bounded` before starting a solve.

findings.title: request.post is answered by a GET navigation and postData is parsed then discarded
findings.detail: `FsReq.post_data` is deserialized purely for wire-completeness and marked `#[allow(dead_code)]` (apps/reader/src-tauri/src/cloudflare.rs:96-99), and `WebviewSolver` always performs a plain navigation (`WebviewUrl::External(url)`, :457) regardless of `cmd`. Real FlareSolverr replays the form POST in the browser. The engine sends `"request.post"` with a form body whenever the original request was a POST (CloudflareInterceptor.kt builds `postData` from the FormBody). For most CF deployments the clearance is host-scoped so a GET to the same URL still yields it, which is why this is low — but a source whose gated endpoint is POST-only will answer the GET with 404/405, no challenge JS will run, and the solve will time out. Any method other than GET/POST (e.g. `request.head`) is rejected outright at :193-195; real FlareSolverr behaves the same way, so that part is parity, not divergence.
findings.failure_scenario: A source whose search/page-list endpoint is POST-only sits behind CF. The engine sends `request.post` with `postData`; the shim GETs the URL, receives a 405 page with no challenge, polls fruitlessly for 45 s, and returns an error — the source is permanently hosted-only on desktop too.
findings.fix_sketch: For `cmd == "request.post"`, navigate to the URL's origin (or the referring page) to obtain host-scoped clearance rather than GETting a POST-only path; or inject and submit a form via `eval` using the parsed `postData`. At minimum, record the limitation in the module docs and in §8b instead of silently ignoring the field.

verdicts.reason: Reproduced from source. suwayomi_ios.rs:69-71 defines JVM_THREAD_STACK = 16 MiB with the stated Zero rationale, and it is applied at :575 to exactly one thread (the VM owner, which calls JNI_CreateJavaVM and therefore keeps its own 16 MiB native stack — -Xss does not govern an attaching/primordial thread). The option list at :378-379 passes -Xss1m, which is the ONLY stack knob for every thread HotSpot spawns itself; grep confirms no -XX:ThreadStackSize or any other stack setting anywhere in src-tauri/src/*.rs. Desktop (suwayomi.rs:257-266) indeed sets no -Xss and is a JIT VM. The path is reachable on the intended target (lib.rs:20 gates the module to real iOS devices, which is the shipping path of the plan), and the extension-install scenario is real: local-suwayomi-backend.ts:289-345 installs the MangaDex extension on-device via fetchExtensions/updateExtension(install:true) (dex2jar on an engine worker thread), and composite-backend.ts:352-404 does memoize failures into localUnusable, so a single SOE would silently poison works. No guard, caller, or other layer compensates. Caveat: suwayomi_ios.rs cannot be compiled or run on this aarch64-Linux host, so this is source-text + HotSpot/Zero-semantics reasoning, not an executed reproduction; the SOE itself remains plausible-but-unmeasured, which is why this stays a robustness/tuning finding rather than a proven defect.
verdicts.corrected_detail: Confirmed with two corrections to the original framing. (1) The fix sketch's "drop -Xss1m" option is a no-op, not a fix: HotSpot's BSD/aarch64 default thread stack (os::Bsd::default_stack_size for java threads) is already 1M, so removing the flag leaves the same 1 MiB. Only RAISING it (e.g. -Xss4m/-Xss8m) changes behaviour. (2) The concern is sharper than stated under Zero: Zero carves a separate ZeroStack for Java frames out of roughly half the thread's ABI stack (ZeroStack::suggest_size ≈ abi_stack_available/2), while the CppInterpreter main loop simultaneously recurses on the remaining C stack per Java call — so -Xss1m buys ~512 KB of effective Java-frame depth on engine worker threads, versus the 16 MiB the module deliberately gives its own VM thread for exactly this reason. Cost of raising is low and should be said explicitly: thread stacks are virtual and lazily committed, and iOS jetsam accounts dirty pages, so an unbounded-looking -Xss8m adds little real footprint. The StackOverflowError in the failure scenario (dex2jar/ASM during the first MangaDex extension install, poisoning composite-backend's localUnusable set) is plausible but unmeasured — typical Kotlin-coroutine + Javalin + dex2jar depths sit in the low hundreds of frames, which is borderline at ~512 KB — so this is a robustness/tuning gap to resolve with an N4.3 on-device measurement, not a demonstrated crash.

verdicts.reason: Independently reproduced from source. In apps/reader/src-tauri/src/suwayomi_ios.rs, JNI_CreateJavaVM at :403-409 attaches the calling thread as the VM's non-daemon "main" JavaThread, and all five post-create error returns (:427, :435, :442, :447, :456) exit without DetachCurrentThread or DestroyJavaVM. `grep -rn "Detach|catch_unwind|Drop for" suwayomi_ios.rs` matches nothing, so there is no RAII guard or epilogue anywhere. The caller closure (:576-583) only logs + degrades and returns, so the spawned `suwayomi-jvm` thread terminates while attached; the JoinHandle is dropped at :584, so the pthread is detached and its stack is reclaimed at exit. The path is reachable: lib.rs:20-22 cfg-maps this module for real iOS devices and lib.rs:256 calls suwayomi::start() unconditionally in setup (the PUBLIC_KOMIKA_NATIVE_ENGINE flag gates USE, not boot), and nothing ever reclaims the VM afterwards (stop_and_wait deliberately skips DestroyJavaVM; boot_attempted latches so there is no second attempt). The code claim, the reachability and the "no cleanup" claim all hold; only the crash mechanism and the proposed fix are mis-stated (see corrected_detail). NOTE: suwayomi_ios.rs cannot be compiled on this aarch64-Linux host, so this is static source reasoning plus JNI/HotSpot semantics, not an executed reproduction.
verdicts.corrected_detail: The defect is real but the stated crash mechanism is speculative and the fix sketch is wrong. (1) Mechanism: after returning from a JNI call the thread has no last_Java_frame anchor, so HotSpot's GC/safepoint root scan of that JavaThread walks its C-heap JNIHandleBlock/handle area, not the (now-freed) native stack — the described "safepoint/GC stack-scan walks the freed stack -> SIGSEGV" is not the likely failure. What IS certain: the JNI spec requires an attached native thread to detach before exiting, HotSpot never auto-detaches (no pthread_key destructor), so the JavaThread stays in the Threads list forever with a dead pthread_t/OSThread. Concrete, non-speculative consequences: (a) the VM is never torn down — it keeps a reserved 256 MB heap (-Xmx256m) plus GC/VM/internal threads alive for the whole app lifetime while the app has already degraded to the hosted fallback, which on iOS materially raises jetsam-kill probability for zero benefit; (b) any later VM operation that touches the dead thread's OSThread (signal-based handshake, thread dump/JFR, pthread_kill) is undefined behaviour and is the plausible crash route, not GC stack scanning; (c) it is exactly the terminal-degrade path taken when the bundle/classpath is wrong, i.e. the most likely first-run state on a real device. (2) Fix: DetachCurrentThread is the wrong call here — the JNI Invocation API states the VM-creating ("main") thread cannot be detached and must call DestroyJavaVM to unload the VM. The epilogue should call ((**vm).DestroyJavaVM.unwrap())(vm) before returning Err; at that point the erroring thread is the only non-daemon thread, so DestroyJavaVM returns promptly, detaches it and reclaims the 256 MB reservation. Structuring the post-create body as an inner closure whose Result flows through one cleanup epilogue (optionally wrapped in catch_unwind) is still the right shape, though the panic risk is negligible: the only unwrap()s in that region are CString::new on string literals.

verdicts.reason: Independently reproduced from source. The readiness task at suwayomi_ios.rs:592-613 is a one-shot `tauri::async_runtime::spawn`: on Ok it calls `set_ready` and the task ends. Grepping the whole file, the only other `spawn` is the JVM owner thread; there is no timer, loop or re-check. `Inner.state` is mutated only by `set_ready`/`transition`/`degrade`/`stop_and_wait`, and after Ready the sole remaining caller is `stop_and_wait` (app exit) — so nothing can move the state off Ready for a dead engine. `base_url()` (:187-194) and `ready_endpoint()` (:196-203) gate purely on `state == Ready`, so they keep handing out the dead port. Desktop contrast confirmed at suwayomi.rs:421-423 (`status = child.wait()` -> `transition(Degraded, "engine exited unexpectedly")`), and the heap asymmetry is real (-Xmx256m at suwayomi_ios.rs:378 vs -Xmx512m at suwayomi.rs:261). The JS consequence is confirmed too: local-suwayomi-backend.ts:113-122 returns true iff `state === 'ready'`, composite-backend.ts:352 gates on it and :404 adds the work to `localUnusable` — a Set that is never deleted from or cleared anywhere in the repo, so the degradation is permanent for the session while `suwayomi_status` still reports `{state:'ready', lastError:null}`. No guard, caller or other layer handles it. Path is reachable: `start()` is the normal ios boot path and set_ready is its success branch. Caveat: suwayomi_ios.rs is cfg-gated to real iOS devices and cannot be compiled on this aarch64 Linux host, so this is source-text/control-flow reasoning only — but the argument is purely about which functions mutate `state` and who calls them, which compilation would not change.
verdicts.corrected_detail: Confirmed as written, with one addition the original finding missed: the in-process VM does have exactly ONE observable death signal today, and it is dropped on the floor. `run_jvm` (suwayomi_ios.rs:370-469) blocks in `DestroyJavaVM` after Java `main` returns and then returns `Ok(())` once every non-daemon engine thread has exited — i.e. the engine is definitively dead — logging `"in-process JVM destroyed (all non-daemon threads exited)"` at :468. But the spawning closure at :576-583 is `if let Err(e) = run_jvm(&jar, &data_dir) { ... sup_jvm.degrade(e) }`, so the `Ok(())` (engine-died) path performs no state transition at all and `Inner.state` stays `Ready`. That makes the fix cheaper than the sketch implies: (a) degrade unconditionally when `run_jvm` returns, whatever the variant (e.g. `sup_jvm.degrade("engine stopped")` on the Ok arm) — this catches clean/total engine death for free; plus (b) the sketched low-frequency `aboutServer` heartbeat after `set_ready` for the partial-death cases (Javalin thread died, OOM killed the HTTP acceptor) where non-daemon threads linger and `DestroyJavaVM` never returns. Both are needed: (a) alone misses partial death, (b) alone is the general case but costs a poll. Severity `medium` is right — the app still functionally falls back to hosted content (composite-backend.ts:420-429 catches and falls through), so this is an observability + permanent-per-work-memo/latency defect rather than an outage, but it silently defeats the zero-Worker goal on iOS with no signal to the user, the logs, or the runbook.

verdicts.reason: Code text is accurate (suwayomi_ios.rs:370-380 sets only -Djava.class.path, rootDir, -Djava.awt.headless, -Xmx256m, -Xss1m; suwayomi_image ~:711-716 does share crate::image_fetch_semaphore(), 6 x 32 MiB from lib.rs:33/40/45), but the finding's substance does not hold. (1) "Direct buffers unbounded" is false: with -XX:MaxDirectMemorySize unset, HotSpot defaults it to Runtime.maxMemory(), i.e. the -Xmx256m already in the list, so direct memory is implicitly capped by the very flag the finding calls "the only" cap. (2) "Code cache unbounded" is false for this VM: build.rs:54 links jre-ios/aarch64-ios/lib/zero/libjvm.a and the module header (suwayomi_ios.rs:6) + scripts/build-ios-jvm.sh:3,181 confirm an interpreter-only Zero (NO-JIT) OpenJDK — there is no C1/C2 and therefore no growing JIT code cache; ReservedCodeCacheSize is inapplicable. (3) Per-thread stacks ARE bounded by the -Xss1m that is present, and no JVM flag exists to bound thread count, so that half of the fix_sketch is not actionable. (4) The stated failure scenario cannot be shown to occur: the finding's own itemization sums to roughly 256 (heap) + ~100 (metaspace) + <=256 (direct, implicitly capped) + 192 (worst-case image buffers) ~= 800 MB, and the ~149 MB jimage is a clean file-backed mmap which iOS phys_footprint (the metric jetsam meters) excludes; WKWebView is a separate process with its own accounting. Foreground jetsam limits on 4 GB iPhones are ~2 GB, so no crossing is demonstrated. (5) The proposed fix is a live regression risk on an untestable target: -XX:MaxMetaspaceSize=128m against Kotlin + Suwayomi + per-extension classloaders plausibly triggers OutOfMemoryError: Metaspace and kills the engine outright, and MaxDirectMemorySize=64m tightens a limit that is currently 256m. The only true residual is that metaspace alone is uncapped — a speculative tuning nit bounded in practice by installed-extension count, not a medium perf defect. Confidence caveat: suwayomi_ios.rs is #[cfg(target_os="ios")] + non-simulator ABI and cannot be compiled or executed on this aarch64-Linux host, so points 1-3 rest on HotSpot/Zero semantics plus the repo's own build config rather than on runtime observation; no device RSS measurement exists in either direction, which argues against confirming a memory-pressure claim.
